statement: Let $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ be a prime, let $\varepsilon = (t + u\sqrt{p})/2$ be the [fundamental unit](c:fundamental-unit) of the [real quadratic field](c:real-quadratic-field) $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p})$, and let $h$ be its [class number](c:ideal-class-group). Then $p \nmid t$, the [Bernoulli number](c:bernoulli-number) $B_{(p-1)/2}$ is $p$-integral, and $uh/t \equiv B_{(p-1)/2} \pmod p$.

hypotheses.text: The number $p$ is a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$.
The real number $\varepsilon = (t + u\sqrt{p})/2 > 1$, with $t, u$ integers, is the [fundamental unit](c:fundamental-unit) of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p})$.
The integer $h$ is the [class number](c:ideal-class-group) of the [real quadratic field](c:real-quadratic-field) $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p})$.

conclusion: The integer $t$ is prime to $p$, $B_{(p-1)/2}$ is $p$-integral, and $uh/t \equiv B_{(p-1)/2} \pmod p$ in $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$.

proofs.name: p-adic class number formula
proofs.slogan: Compute the $p$-adic $L$-value $L_p(1,\chi)$ once through the class number formula and once through Bernoulli interpolation, then compare.
proofs.scope: The whole congruence, for every $p \ge 5$ (all primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$). Variants for other discriminants and for higher powers of $p$ are not covered.

roles.why: The condition $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ makes the quadratic character $\chi$ even, with $\chi = \omega^{n}$ for $n = (p-1)/2$.
The unit $\varepsilon$ and its coordinates $t, u$ give the $p$-adic logarithm that is expanded in the congruence.
The class number $h$ is the factor that the class number formula puts in front of the logarithm of $\varepsilon$.

steps.slogan: Express $\varepsilon^{2h}$ as a product of the factors $1-\zeta^a$.
steps.detail: Let $\chi$ be the Legendre symbol, an even [Dirichlet character](c:dirichlet-character), and $g = \sum_a \chi(a)\zeta^a = \sqrt{p}$ its [Gauss sum](c:gauss-sum). The formula $L(1,\chi) = 2h\log\varepsilon/\sqrt{p}$ and the expansion $L(1,\chi) = -p^{-1/2}\sum_a \chi(a)\log|1-\zeta^a|$ give $2h\log\varepsilon = -\sum_a \chi(a)\log|1-\zeta^a|$. The arguments of the factors $1-\zeta^a$ cancel, because $a \mapsto p-a$ preserves $\chi$, so $\varepsilon^{2h} = \prod_a (1-\zeta^a)^{-\chi(a)}$.

steps.slogan: Convert the product into $L_p(1,\chi) = 2h\log_p\varepsilon/g$ with Leopoldt's formula.
steps.detail: The product is an identity in the field of [p-adic numbers](c:p-adic-number) $\mathbb{Q}_p(\zeta)$, so $2h\log_p\varepsilon = -\sum_a \chi(a)\log_p(1-\zeta^a)$, with $\log_p p = 0$. Leopoldt's formula for the even character $\chi$ of conductor $p$ says $L_p(1,\chi) = -(g/p)\sum_a \chi(a)\log_p(1-\zeta^a)$. Since $g^2 = p$, this is $L_p(1,\chi) = 2h\log_p\varepsilon/g$.

steps.slogan: Shift $L_p(1,\chi)$ to $L_p(1-n,\chi)$ modulo $p$ with the power series of the [L-function](c:l-function).
steps.detail: Because $\chi \ne 1$, the $p$-adic $L$-function is $L_p(s,\chi) = F((1+p)^s - 1)$ for a power series $F \in \mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$. For $s \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ the argument $(1+p)^s - 1$ lies in $p\mathbb{Z}_p$, so $L_p(s,\chi) \equiv F(0) \pmod p$. Hence $L_p(1,\chi) \equiv L_p(1-n,\chi) \pmod p$ for every $n \ge 1$.

steps.slogan: Evaluate $L_p(1-n,\chi)$ at $n=(p-1)/2$ with the Bernoulli interpolation formula.
steps.detail: Euler's criterion gives $\chi = \omega^n$, so $\chi\omega^{-n} = 1$ and the interpolation formula reads $L_p(1-n,\chi) = -(1-p^{n-1})B_n/n$. The index $n$ is even and $p-1 \nmid n$, so the [Bernoulli number](c:bernoulli-number) $B_n$ is $p$-integral. As $n \equiv -1/2 \pmod p$ and $n \ge 2$, this value is $\equiv 2B_{(p-1)/2} \pmod p$.

steps.slogan: Expand the $p$-adic logarithm of $\varepsilon$ as an odd power series in $g$.
steps.detail: Write $\varepsilon = (t/2)(1+xg)$ with $x = u/t$; here $p \nmid t$ because $t^2 - pu^2 = \pm 4$. The conjugate $\varepsilon' = (t/2)(1-xg)$ has $\varepsilon\varepsilon' = \pm 1$, so $\log_p\varepsilon = \tfrac12\log_p\frac{1+xg}{1-xg} = \sum_{k \ge 0}(xg)^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$. Dividing by $g$ gives $x\sum_k (x^2p)^k/(2k+1)$, and each term with $k \ge 1$ is divisible by $p$ since $p \ge 5$, so $\log_p\varepsilon/g \equiv u/t \pmod p$.

steps.slogan: Compare the two values of $L_p(1,\chi)$ modulo $p$ and divide by 2.
steps.detail: Steps 2 and 5 give $L_p(1,\chi) \equiv 2hu/t \pmod p$, and steps 3 and 4 give $L_p(1,\chi) \equiv 2B_{(p-1)/2} \pmod p$. Since $p$ is odd, $uh/t \equiv B_{(p-1)/2} \pmod p$; the claims $p \nmid t$ and $p$-integrality were shown in steps 5 and 4.

concepts.c:fundamental-unit: Its $p$-adic logarithm carries the coordinates $t$ and $u$ into the congruence.
concepts.c:real-quadratic-field: The field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p})$ lies in $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$, so its unit is a cyclotomic product.
concepts.c:ideal-class-group: Its order $h$ multiplies the logarithm of the unit in the class number formula.
concepts.c:bernoulli-number: The $p$-adic $L$-function takes a Bernoulli number as its value at $1-n$.
concepts.c:dirichlet-character: The quadratic character $\chi$ is even and equals $\omega^{(p-1)/2}$.
concepts.c:gauss-sum: The Gauss sum $g$ equals $\sqrt{p}$ and joins the character to roots of unity.
concepts.c:p-adic-number: The logarithm, the $L$-function and the congruence all live in $\mathbb{Q}_p(\zeta)$.
concepts.c:l-function: The $p$-adic $L$-function links the class number side to the Bernoulli side.

source.note: A modern derivation from Leopoldt's p-adic class number formula and the interpolation of Bernoulli numbers, as in Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, 2nd ed., Springer GTM 83 (1997), chapter 5. The original proof (Ankeny, Artin and Chowla, Annals of Mathematics 56 (1952), 479-493) predates p-adic L-functions and argues differently.
